# ai-search-visibility-skills

Skills this pack ships:

- `ai-visibility-audit` - six-pillar AI visibility scoring for a site.
- `robots-ai-crawler-audit` - checks `robots-txt` and `well-known` paths for AI crawler access.
- `sitemap-discovery-audit` - sitemap and `llms-txt` discovery, including non-default filenames.
- `schema-markup-audit` - `json-ld` structured data, `x-default` and `en-nz` hreflang pairs.
- `ai-search-remediation-plan` - turns ranked findings into prioritized tickets.

Every audit is read-only. Nothing in this pack writes to the target site, opens a pull
request, or submits anything to a third-party console.
cases.guide:
# Prompt Guide

## Quick start

```
Run ai-visibility-audit against https://example.com and give me the prioritized action plan.
```

## Giving useful context

- The target URL, because the pack classifies the site type from it before choosing checks.
- Whether you already have analytics access, because that changes measured vs. derived findings.
- Who reads the report, because an executive summary and a developer ticket list are different deliverables.

## Structuring a complex or multi-phase request

```
# Instructions
1. Audit https://example.com with ai-visibility-audit.
2. Hand the ranked findings to ai-search-remediation-plan.

# Context
Ecommerce storefront, 400 SKUs, no server logs available.
```

Put the bulk material first and the actual ask last.

## Good vs. less-effective prompt examples

Less effective:

```
check my seo
```

More effective:

```
Run ai-visibility-audit against https://example.com and report Pillar 1 findings only.
```

Naming the skill and the scope stops the run from wandering across all six pillars.

Less effective:

```
also fix it
```

More effective:

```
Convert the critical findings into P0 tickets using ai-search-remediation-plan.
```

Naming the downstream skill produces tickets instead of prose.

## Known limitations to mention explicitly

- Hydrated-DOM verification (#102) is not on main yet: the fix is open in PR #104 and unmerged, so raw-HTML false negatives are still possible today.
- Sitemap discovery misses non-default filenames (#103), fix pending in #105.

## Where to go deeper

See the pack's SKILL.md and README.md.
